newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly lower on Tuesday on profit-taking with interest sluggish, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 21,740 yuan per tonne, losing 70 yuan. It opened at 21,730 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 21,710 and a high of 21,790.
February rose 20 to 21,620, March fell 60 to 21,620, April 50 to 21,670, and June 80 to 21,750.
Combined volume rose to 20,600 tonnes from 16,630.
Traders said profit-taking dominated trading with the approach of the Chinese new year holiday, which begins on February 3.

"Most investors had little interest in building fresh positions and were eager to liquidate their positions at appropriate prices," one trader said. "A lack of market-moving news kept copper in a narrow range."
"Copper will continue to trade slowly for the next few days because investors are not interested," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended down. February was unchanged at 15,420, March fell 10 to 15,650, and April 40 to 15,760.
